definition: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B is the smallest of the DeepSeek-R1 distillations and the model the archive's length-reduction work uses when it wants a second scale alongside the 7B. It is filed as a model; earlier wiki text said the wiki had no kind for one, which is no longer true. Across the sources it plays two roles. As a training target it is the small sibling: Ada-R1 merges long-CoT and short-CoT versions of it under bi-level preference training across AIME25, MATH500, GSM8K, OlympiadBench and Minerva Math, though its headline 50.93% length cut at a 1.65-point accuracy cost is measured on the 7B; ShorterBetter trains it on 40K DeepScaleR-preview problems against a per-problem target set by the shortest correct sampled response, reporting 50%-80% output-length reduction across the 1.5B/7B pair in and out of domain; ChainPrune reports its own numbers on it directly, raising AIME24 accuracy 0.3104 to 0.3292 and AMC23 0.7016 to 0.7250 while cutting AMC23 chain length from 167 to 87 steps. As a subject of measurement, Bloom's Taxonomy profiling gives it the highest Evaluating share of the R1 distillations at 21.0% against 9.3% for the Llama-8B distillation, with Applying at 35.6%. No source reports its architecture or standalone capability figures beyond these runs.

evidence.note: Trains a 1.5B reasoning model to emit one of three mode tokens (NoThink, Short, Long) as the very first token of its response and to reason under that mode's budget, learned end-to-end inside GRPO with no separate router.
evidence.title: Learning When to Think: Adaptive Reasoning for Test-Time Compute Allocation

evidence.note: ChainPrune merges semantically equivalent steps from 16 sampled reasoning paths into a tree, picks Pareto-dominant short paths as DPO preference data, and fine-tunes with an added NLL term, cutting tokens 28.1% and reasoning steps 26.8% on two R1-distilled models without losing accuracy.
evidence.title: ChainPrune: Evaluating and Reducing Redundancy in Long Chain-of-Thought Reasoning

evidence.note: The paper segments LRM reasoning traces into cognitive steps with Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, labels each step with one of Bloom's six levels, and uses the resulting level proportions and 6x6 transition matrix to profile seven reasoning models and to predict solution correctness.
evidence.title: Cognitive Profiling of LRMs' Reasoning Traces Using Bloom's Taxonomy

evidence.note: CAT (Confidence-Adaptive Thinking) uses self-certainty -- the KL divergence of a reasoning trajectory's per-token predictive distribution from uniform, an intrinsic model signal requiring no external labels -- to build preference pairs and a confidence-weighted preference-optimization loss (CWPO) that compresses reasoning on problems the model is confident about while preserving deliberation on uncertain ones, beating three efficient-reasoning baselines (OverThink, DAST, ConCISE) on accuracy-at-compression across three LRMs and three benchmarks.
evidence.title: CAT: Confidence-Adaptive Thinking for Efficient Reasoning of Large Reasoning Models

evidence.note: Identifies 'length shift' -- reasoning models progressively generate longer responses on already-correctly-solved (zero-gradient) training queries during RLVR, because reasoning-word emission learned for hard problems generalizes indiscriminately to easy ones -- and fixes it with Dynamic Outlier Truncation (DOT), a training-time RL intervention that truncates only the statistical outlier-length tail of all-correct rollout groups (affecting <0.5% of responses) while leaving hard queries unconstrained, cutting AIME-24 token usage 78% while increasing accuracy over the initial policy and beating prior efficient-reasoning methods.
evidence.title: Anti-Length Shift: Dynamic Outlier Truncation for Training Efficient Reasoning Models

evidence.note: LEASH formulates reasoning-length control as a constrained RL optimization (maximize task reward subject to an expected-length constraint) solved via a Lagrangian primal-dual method with a one-sided length penalty, letting the penalty coefficient lambda self-tighten or self-relax based on real-time constraint violation rather than requiring manual tuning, and reduces average reasoning length by up to 62.7% (1.5B model) or 26.2% (4B model) while maintaining or improving accuracy on in-domain math and out-of-domain (GPQA, MMLU-Pro) benchmarks, outperforming fixed-penalty and prior length-control baselines.
evidence.title: LEASH: Adaptive Length Penalty and Reward Shaping for Efficient Large Reasoning Model

evidence.note: Ada-R1 merges a long-CoT and a short-CoT model into one hybrid, then applies two levels of preference training so the model first picks a reasoning style per problem and then prefers the shorter correct trace within that style, cutting average reasoning length by about 51% on five maths datasets.
evidence.title: Ada-R1: Hybrid-CoT via Bi-Level Adaptive Reasoning Optimization

evidence.note: ShorterBetter takes the length of the shortest correct response in a sampled group as a per-problem target and rewards the model for matching it, cutting output length by 50%-80% on DeepSeek-Distill-Qwen-1.5B/7B.
evidence.title: ShorterBetter: Guiding Reasoning Models to Find Optimal Inference Length for Efficient Reasoning

name: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B
